spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The main mathematical compression is the passage from an admissible non-negative trigonometric polynomial to one scalar objective: its coefficients determine an implicit angle and a few summary quantities, and these determine the asymptotic zero-free constant. The search can therefore optimize a finite witness without repeatedly manipulating the full analytic argument.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For P_K(x)=sum_{k=0}^K b_k cos(kx), the conditions b_k>=0, b_1>b_0, and P_K(x)>=0 for every real x imply an asymptotic zero-free region with denominator R_2 (log|t|)^(2/3)(log log|t|)^(1/3). The source defines theta as the unique solution in (0,pi/2) of b_0 sin^2(theta)=b_1(1-theta cot(theta)), sets b=sum_{k=1}^K b_k=P_K(0)-b_0, and computes R_2 from theta, b, b_0, and B in (8.2).
directed.conceptual_reading: The polynomial is an auxiliary proof object whose large coefficient list is compressed to the statistics that control the final region. This exposes a concrete optimization direction: improve the theorem constant by varying an admissible polynomial while preserving the analytic interface summarized by theta and b.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Equation (8.1) bridges coefficient geometry to an angle, and (8.2) bridges that angle and coefficient mass to R_2. Together they turn selection of a proof auxiliary into finite-dimensional objective minimization.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The implication is only for sufficiently large |t| and only for polynomials satisfying all three admissibility conditions. A lower computed R_2 does not by itself establish admissibility, optimality, or an all-height zero-free region.
directed.uncertainty: The mathematical dependency is clear in the prose, but the typeset factors and exponents in (8.2) are display-dependent and should be checked against the rendered page before exact reuse.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The decisive move is to search over a spectral factor g rather than directly over trigonometric coefficients. Writing the candidate as a normalized squared modulus makes global non-negativity invariant under every parameter update, converting an infinite family of pointwise constraints into a built-in property.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For coefficients c_0=1,c_1,...,c_K, the source sets g(x)=sum_{k=0}^K c_k e^(ikx) and P_K(x)=|g(x)|^2 divided by sum_{j=0}^K c_j^2. Then b_0=1 and each b_k for k>0 is a scaled kth autocorrelation of the c-sequence, so P_K(x)>=0 for all x. Positive random initial c_k also give b_k>=0; the remaining condition b_1>b_0 is tested before annealing begins.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is constraint-preserving parameterization: a difficult functional inequality is absorbed into the representation, leaving only finite coefficient inequalities and the objective to test. The autocorrelations expose how local changes to c propagate to the Fourier coefficients used by the proof.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The spectral factor g is the bridge object between unconstrained finite parameters and a globally non-negative trigonometric polynomial. Its autocorrelation map supplies the b_k needed by the zero-free objective while the squared-modulus form preserves non-negativity.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The representation guarantees P_K>=0, but arbitrary signed c-updates do not guarantee every b_k>=0 or b_1>b_0; those constraints still require explicit rejection tests. Simulated annealing remains a heuristic and gives no global optimum certificate.
directed.uncertainty: The factorization and its role are legible, but the exact normalization and displayed autocorrelation fraction should be scan-checked before numerical implementation.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The search uses two levels of objective fidelity. A relatively cheap asymptotic constant supports broad exploration, after which promising candidates are rescored and refined for the more expensive all-height constant; this makes the intermediate polynomial, not merely the best score, reusable across objectives.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: An iteration perturbs one c_k by s in [-S,S], updates the b_k in O(K), rejects any candidate with a negative b_k or b_1<=b_0, and otherwise recomputes theta by Newton's method and R_2. Improvements are accepted and worse moves are accepted with probability exp(-Delta R_2/T); temperatures and step sizes decrease. Searches over degrees 10 through 72 found a degree-46 polynomial with R_2=48.1587921551117. For the costlier all-height R_1 objective, searches were restricted, while a larger asymptotic search retained candidates for R_1 rescoring; a degree-40 candidate was then further annealed directly for R_1.
directed.conceptual_reading: The protocol separates feasibility, exploration, and target evaluation. Cooling permits escape from local minima, while proxy-to-target transfer uses R_2 to explore a larger space and R_1 to select or refine candidates when direct evaluation is costly.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The maintained c-vector and incrementally updated autocorrelations make each move computationally local; Newton's solution for theta completes the bridge to the analytic objective. Archived polynomials bridge the asymptotic search to the all-height search even though the two rankings differ.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The reported schedules, degree ranges, and best values are computational search evidence, not proof of global optimality. A polynomial good for R_2 need not be best for R_1, as the degree-40 example explicitly shows.
directed.uncertainty: The prose supports the algorithm and reported outcomes, but exact coefficients occur in subsequent tables and the searches were not independently reproduced here.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Kadiri's iteration is organized around a deliberately constrained smoother: compact support, two derivatives, and Laplace-transform positivity are the functional interfaces the proof needs. Heath-Brown's four parameterized families compress this infinite-dimensional design problem to a small choice of family and parameters.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source attributes the classical zero-free constant R_0=5.69693 to Kadiri's iterative procedure. Its smoothing function f lies in C^2[0,1], has compact support, and has Laplace transform F non-negative on the positive real axis. Four Heath-Brown families are denoted f^(i)_{eta,lambda,theta}, with the displayed scaling f^(i)_{eta,lambda,theta}(t)=eta h^(i)_{lambda,theta}(eta t).
directed.conceptual_reading: The auxiliary smoother packages several analytic requirements into one object. Selecting within a known admissible family preserves the proof interface while making improvement a parameter-selection problem rather than unrestricted function invention.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The functions h^(i) and their scale parameter eta bridge finite family parameters to compactly supported smoothers whose Laplace positivity can enter the zero-free iteration.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This unit specifies the required properties and family-level parameterization, not the full iteration, the proofs of admissibility, or a comparison among the four families. Membership in a family does not itself identify the best zero-free constant.
directed.uncertainty: The family definition continues after page-layout-interleaved material in the extraction. The prose requirements are reliable here, but the exact displayed notation and normalization should be checked on the rendered page.

The bullet-point changes expose the interface obligations that must be rechecked when one component is swapped.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source combines the degree-16 admissible polynomial from earlier work, the first smoother from (9.2), and RH verification to T_0=3*10^12. It fixes lambda=1 and theta=1.13489, modifies d_1 and g_1, uses a stated cubic upper bound for exp(y) on the needed theta range, initializes the iteration between 5 and 5.573412, and reports checks that C(eta)<=0 on [0,1/(5 log(3*10^12))] and that K(w) is increasing on [0,1]. Seven iterations yield R_0=5.5586904517.
directed.conceptual_reading: The proof method behaves modularly only after compatibility conditions are discharged. The new constant is a synthesis of independently developed inputs, while the altered identities, inequality range, and monotonicity/error checks are the glue that makes their composition legitimate.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The prior iterative scheme is the shared interface; T_0 supplies a certified boundary height, the trigonometric polynomial supplies positivity-weighted coefficients, and the smoother supplies transformed weights. The listed adjustments translate the new smoother into the old iteration.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The full iteration is imported from cited prior work, so this span is not a self-contained verification. The side conditions and final number are reported computational facts here, and combining components does not show which interaction accounts for each part of the gain.
directed.uncertainty: The bullet-point conditions are legible and source-grounded, but their numerical verification was not reproduced. Exact interval endpoints and formulas should retain this source provenance.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: This short unit performs two useful sensitivity checks: a smoother swap estimates the marginal value of that component, while varying the hypothetical verified RH height turns an external future certificate into a response curve for the same proof mechanism.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Using the fourth rather than the chosen first Heath-Brown smoother gives the larger value R_0=5.5608403, so the first-family choice lowers R_0 by about 2.15*10^-3 in this setup. The Xylouris function was not investigated because its earlier marginal benefit was very small. Holding theta=1.13489 and the degree-16 polynomial fixed, the authors also computed projected R_0 values for hypothetical future RH verification heights T_0 up to 10^15.
directed.conceptual_reading: The smoother comparison is an ablation of one proof component, and the future-height calculation is sensitivity analysis. Together they separate a modest design gain from the predictable benefit of strengthening an upstream verified boundary.
directed.representation_or_bridge: R_0 serves as the common output metric for both interventions. The fixed polynomial and theta make the smoother swap interpretable, while T_0 acts as an external certificate parameter that can be propagated through the unchanged iteration.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The ablation is not exhaustive: the Xylouris option was omitted and interactions with re-optimizing theta or the polynomial are not tested. The future values are conditional projections, not zero-free-region improvements already established.
directed.uncertainty: Superscript placement in the extracted smoother names is layout-sensitive. The projection table lies outside the exact unit and contains rounded computational outputs, so only the stated sensitivity setup is secure here.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The proposed extension reframes one global bound as an envelope assembled from many locally overlapping zero-free shapes. Its key missing object is sharply identified: a finite-region exclusion oracle strong enough to certify every transition gap at enormous heights.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source states that a zero-free bound on a short interval [T_0-1,T_0) can, under suitable conditions, be propagated to all t>=T_0. It proposes a sequence nu_j(t)=1/[r_j(log t)^(phi_j)(log log t)^(1-phi_j)] with phi_j>2/3, choosing parameters so each bound improves the preceding one on a finite interval and their union forms an envelope. A construction with 355 transition regions would lower the Theorem 1.1 constant to 52.74 if all those regions were zero-free. Their heights range from about exp(40000) to exp(5*10^7), beyond what raw computation or current zero-density estimates can completely exclude.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is a local-to-global bootstrap. Each established region would certify the boundary condition needed to activate the next, and the final region would propagate globally; the envelope representation exposes both the potential gain and the exact gaps where induction can fail.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The sequence of log-power profiles nu_j is the bridge between a one-threshold propagation argument and a multi-stage construction. The small rectangles between consecutive profiles are explicit intermediate proof obligations, effectively queries to a presently unavailable zero-exclusion mechanism.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The value 52.74 is conditional on excluding zeros in every one of 355 finite regions and is not an established improvement. Failure of current computation and density estimates to exclude those zeros is a tool limitation, not evidence that zeros occur there.
directed.uncertainty: The construction and obstruction are clear in prose, but the displayed eta substitution and the exact coordinates of region (10.1) are formula-sensitive and should be checked against the rendered page before formal reuse.
